findings.text: the deadline is written into the process environment and never scoped to the replacement image, while reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4661 hands {**os.environ, **plan.environment} to every launched worker, so a crew follow --lifetime started by a descendant of an armed follower adopts its ancestor's deadline instead of its own: reproduced with the variable set five seconds ahead, the arming ended by itself at five seconds with its own follower-end line and exit 0 while the same arming without the variable was still running at eleven seconds (probe log: runs/r-20260923T150322975181-review-of-lifetime-survives-reload/logs/probe-inheritance.log), and an inherited deadline already in the past ends such an arming immediately.

the plan's headline measured figure "1 passed in 10.71 s" has no log behind it — no log in the run directory carries that gate-alone figure, since logs/gate.log records the combined run (3 passed in 30.83 s) under a revision line naming 12155ff8 with "working tree: reckon/cli.py modified" — so the number a reader would check is prose in the plan, repeated at docs/evidence/archive/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor-landed.html:348; the claim itself is sound: I re-ran the gate alone at the reviewed head's clean tree and it passed in 12.10 s.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against base 12155ff8 — bc229de1 adds the carried-deadline reader and the carrying/spending branch in crew follow plus a 264-line gate; ae1f309e appends the §8 landing record to the plan, the cumulative anchor to the archive and a two-panel figure; the mechanism is an absolute epoch in the process environment, set only on a fresh arming and spent by every replacement, and reckon/cli.py:1927-1928 turns the remainder into a monotonic deadline, which is what lets it survive the image replacement.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when at docs/plans/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor.html:335-342 names tests/test_follow_lifetime_survives_reload.py arming the real follower with --lifetime 6s over a temporary RECKON_HOME, forcing one reload about three seconds in and requiring the follower-end line and exit status 0 within eight seconds of the original arm; the landed test asserts exactly that (tests/test_follow_lifetime_survives_reload.py:216-264), the run's gate log records the gate passing with tests/test_follow_lifetime.py's 2 passed beside it, and I re-ran the named test alone against the reviewed head's clean tree: 1 passed in 12.10 s.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a follower's lifetime deadline is fixed at its first arming and carried unchanged across a source-change reload, and the landed code does that — reckon/cli.py:1659-1674 reads a deadline handed over in the environment and reckon/cli.py:2304-2312 spends only what is left of the original arming instead of anchoring a fresh one, so the instant a replacement ends at is the first arming's.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full at the run directory; it names commits bc229de1 and ae1f309e, the gate and adjacent logs with the base comparison that carries its zero added failures, and a negative_control_log whose first line repeats the dispatch's declared mutation verbatim and whose body is red on exactly that mechanism ("still running 8.0s after its original arm"); the one figure it states but does not log is the gate-alone 10.71 s, reported below as a finding.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node's declared paths are reckon/cli.py, tests/test_follow_lifetime_survives_reload.py, docs/evidence/archive/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor-landed.html, docs/figures/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor and docs/plans/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor.html, and `git show --stat bc229de1 ae1f309e` in the reviewed worktree lands six files, every one of them inside that list, with nothing outside it.

justifications.durability: the load-bearing assertion at tests/test_follow_lifetime_survives_reload.py:255 measures elapsed time from the original arm against an independent bound and was demonstrated red by the declared mutation, and no added assertion compares a test-supplied value against a call to the code under test — but the inherited-deadline path a non-reload child takes carries no assertion, which is the finding at reckon/cli.py:2312.
justifications.evidence: the gate performs the done_when's own measure and confirms the image was replaced from the replacement's own /proc command line (tests/test_follow_lifetime_survives_reload.py:155-175) rather than assuming it, its result is a log the manifest names, and the declared negative control is a red log whose first line repeats the mutation the dispatch declared.
justifications.fit: the change follows the file's idiom with a named constant beside _FOLLOWER_CHECKPOINT_ENV, mechanism-named symbols and no plan or ticket labels, but the reader's docstring at reckon/cli.py:1663-1666 claims the value is "absent for a fresh arming" while the variable is process-global and inherited by every descendant, so the claim holds for the host's shell and is false for a child process's.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/cli.py:2304-2312 spends the carried remainder and writes no new deadline, so a reload never extends the arming the goal describes and a reload past the deadline ends the follower at once.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in `git show --stat bc229de1 ae1f309e` is inside the node's declared write paths, and the one production file touched is the one the plan names, reckon/cli.py.
